headline: L1 Capital built a high-conviction position in Downer after accounting irregularities created an unloved entry point, backing management to deliver >$200m cost-out and margin expansion
reasoning: L1 Capital invested in Downer when accounting irregularities and management changes deterred most investors, leveraging their long familiarity with the company. They identified a quality asset base and conducted rigorous upfront work to determine potential cost savings, concluding north of $200m could be extracted — which has since been realised. They encouraged the company to divest non-core assets at market prices and use proceeds to pay down debt, improving the balance sheet and enabling buybacks. Management has delivered on margin expansion and L1 believe intrinsic value remains well above the current share price, suggesting further upside.
quote: A few years ago, Downer had some accounting irregularities, a change of CEO, a change of CFO. Again, we've been an investor in Downer over the journey at various times for the last two decades really. We knew the company well, but quite naturally, there weren't too many people that were putting their hand up to buy the stock after that had that occurrence of events. So we went in there and we looked at a company that we thought fundamentally had a good quality set of assets. We really were prepared to back the CEO, Peter Tonkins, and the CFO, Mal Ashcroft, and the board to actually turn their company around. They've done a really good job. They have grown the margin of the business over time. They've taken out costs. We did a lot of work at the front end of our investment to actually determine the quantum of costs that we thought could be taken out of the business. We thought it was going to be north of 200 million, which has ultimately played out. We encouraged them to sell non-core assets at the market. We're not appropriately valuing and use those proceeds to pay down debt in order to get the balance sheet into a good shape. Then that's enabled them to subsequently initiate a buyback because the balance sheet's got into a good shape. The intrinsic value of the downer stock in the board's view, which we agree with, is well above the current share price. The margin, importantly, the EBITAR margin of the business continues to expand. That was an example of a win whereby we did the work, we backed the management team, and they've done a really good job. We think there's still a bit more to go.
episode_title: The ‘unloved’ stocks fuelling a 30% year in L1 Capital’s Catalyst Fund

headline: L1 Capital long Downer as cost-out expansion, utilities turnaround and new leadership drive margin improvement toward 4.5% EBITA target by FY25.
reasoning: Downer increased its targeted cost-out program by $75m p.a. to $175m p.a. to be achieved by FY25, and its utilities division returned to profitability in H1 2024. The company reaffirmed it remains on track for at least 4.5% EBITA margins in FY25. Downer continues to explore non-core divestments and is finalising a revised capital allocation strategy. With renewed leadership at Board and senior management levels committed to efficiency and simplification, L1 expects Downer to evolve into a more resilient, lower-risk services business exposed to a growing pipeline of annuity-style contracts. FY24 is seen as a transition year with positive impacts materialising in H2 2024.
quote: Downer (Long +16%) shares strengthened over the quarter as the company announced it was increasing its targeted cost-out program by $75m p.a. to a revised total of $175m p.a. to be achieved by FY25. In addition, the company reported that its utilities division successfully returned to profitability during H1 2024, which, together with the expanded cost-out program, saw Downer reaffirm that it remains on track to achieve target EBITA margins of at least 4.5% in FY25. Downer also continues to explore non-core divestments and to finalise a revised capital allocation strategy. While we continue to expect that FY24 will be a transition year for the company, we expect to begin seeing positive impacts from improvements in the cost base and the utilities division materialise during H2 2024.
episode_title: 2024 Mar L1 Long Short Fund Ltd Quarterly Report
